reader_question: My Dockerfile contains EXPOSE 8080. Does that make http://127.0.0.1:8080 work on the host, or what docker run command do I need? I only want host-local access.
reader_context: Docker Engine 28.0.0 or later on Linux, default bridge/NAT networking and default routing settings. The already-built image is demo-web. Its HTTP server is already listening on 0.0.0.0:8080 inside the container. Host port 8080 is free.

mandatory.claim: EXPOSE documents an intended container port; it does not publish a host port.
Use docker run -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 demo-web to publish host loopback port 8080 to container TCP port 8080.
The loopback host address restricts this published port to the host under the stated Engine version and networking assumptions.

mandatory_qualifications: Do not drop 127.0.0.1 from the command: host-local access is requested.
The application must already listen on the container port; that prerequisite is supplied in the reader context.

optional_source_facts.claim: Without an explicit host address, publishing binds all host addresses by default.
-P publishes exposed ports using ephemeral host ports rather than the requested fixed mapping.
Before Engine 28.0.0, other hosts on the same L2 segment could reach localhost-published ports; those versions are excluded here.
